# @zakkster/lite-utils

Five standalone bash tools that compare two JavaScript builds through V8's own
traces -- bytecode length, deopts, inline caches, inlining decisions, young-GC
event counts -- and end every run with a fail-closed verdict line
(SAME / DIFF / NO-VERDICT, or WITHIN / OVER, ZERO / NONZERO, REPORTED). Each
tool is one self-contained bash script that drives `node` and reads its trace
output. This is not a JS library: there is no import, no JS API.

## Status

Unreleased. Version 0.0.0; the first release will be 1.0.0. Nothing here is
available from npm yet.

Install (instructions; pick one):

- `npm i -D @zakkster/lite-utils`
- `npm i -D git+https://github.com/PeshoVurtoleta/lite-utils.git`
- copy ONE root script into your project and run it with `bash <script>`; a
  root never sources another file at run time.

After an npm install the commands are in `./node_modules/.bin/`:
`allocation-diff`, `bytecode-budget`, `deopt-diff`, `ic-diff`,
`inlining-budget-diff`.

## Rules for a caller (read first)

- ALWAYS require the `VERDICT <v>` line on stdout, not only the exit code.
- Exit 2 = NO-VERDICT: the tool could not decide and failed closed. It is not
  "no difference". Never treat 2 as success.
- Exit 0 and 1 are verdicts; the verdict word names which (see each tool).
- `--self-test` exit 1 means a `FAIL <label>` line was printed. It is NOT DIFF.
- `-h` / `--help` prints the header and exits 2 (all five). Do not use it as a
  liveness probe that expects 0.
- An unexpected failure inside a tool exits 2 NO-VERDICT, never 1.
- A refused argument exits 2 before any node is spawned, with these named
  exceptions: a `--v8-flags` flag outside the allowlist is refused after one
  `node --v8-options` read; ibd refuses some mode errors after its probes.
- An unknown option exits 2 with a did-you-mean hint.

## Tools

Shared options (each tool's own `-h` is the authority for its subset):
`--node BIN` (default `$NODE`, else `node`; resolved once to an absolute
path), `--v8-flags STR` (runtime allowlist of V8 flags; log / trace / print /
prof flags and node options are refused), `--out DIR` (keep the report and raw
runs), `--runs N` (runs per side; run 1 vs the later runs is the null control),
`--self-test`, `-h`. The tools strip NODE_OPTIONS, NODE_V8_COVERAGE,
NODE_COMPILE_CACHE and NODE_REDIRECT_WARNINGS from every spawn.

### bytecode-budget (bytecode-budget.sh)

Question: how many bytes of bytecode does each NAMED function compile to?

    bytecode-budget.sh [opts] --fn LIST DRIVER                                 # report
    bytecode-budget.sh [opts] --max fn=N[,fn=N] --node-version vX.Y.Z DRIVER   # gate
    bytecode-budget.sh [opts] --diff --fn LIST DRIVER_BEFORE DRIVER_AFTER      # diff
    bytecode-budget.sh [opts] --diff --fn LIST --out DIR --driver FILE --before-ref REF --after-ref REF --module REL   # diff, ref mode
    bytecode-budget.sh [opts] --diff --fn LIST --out DIR --driver FILE --before FILE --after FILE                      # diff, file mode

- Report: exit 0 REPORTED, 2 NO-VERDICT.
- Gate: `--max` limits plus `--node-version` (required; must equal
  `<node> --version` exactly, else NO-VERDICT). Per function WITHIN / OVER;
  exit 0 WITHIN, 1 OVER, 2 NO-VERDICT.
- Diff: compares the length multisets of two drivers (or two staged module
  versions in ref / file mode); exit 0 SAME, 1 DIFF, 2 NO-VERDICT. `--max` is
  refused with `--diff`.
- Ref / file mode needs git. In file mode the "before" file must be a frozen
  copy, not a git-tracked file.
- Tier: DETERMINISTIC on one node binary and one driver; any run-to-run change
  is NO-VERDICT, never OVER or DIFF. The limit values the tool prints are that
  binary's, a measurement of that binary, not a law. Maxima are only valid on
  the node version they were recorded on.

### deopt-diff (deopt-diff.sh)

Question: did the deoptimizations of NAMED functions change (code tier, kind,
reason, as a multiset)?

    deopt-diff.sh [opts] --fn LIST DRIVER_BEFORE DRIVER_AFTER                                  # driver mode
    deopt-diff.sh [opts] --fn LIST --out DIR --driver FILE --before-ref REF --after-ref REF --module REL   # ref mode
    deopt-diff.sh [opts] --fn LIST --out DIR --driver FILE --before FILE --after FILE                     # file mode
    deopt-diff.sh --self-test [--fixtures DIR]

- Exit 0 SAME, 1 DIFF, 2 NO-VERDICT. `--fn` is required.
- A "Tier" section after the function lines is REPORTED and never moves the
  verdict or exit code.
- Tier: the verdict on a user driver is STATISTICAL (deopts follow tier-up
  timing). `--self-test`, `--self-test --fixtures DIR` and the natives pair
  (deopt.mjs vs mono.mjs) are DETERMINISTIC.

### ic-diff (ic-diff.sh)

Question: did the inline-cache states (kind, key, final state) of NAMED
functions change?

    ic-diff.sh [opts] --fn LIST DRIVER_BEFORE DRIVER_AFTER
    ic-diff.sh --self-test

- Driver mode ONLY. There is no ref mode and no file mode.
- Exit 0 SAME, 1 DIFF, 2 NO-VERDICT.
- On node 22 and 24 this tool always ends NO-VERDICT (by design; see Known
  limits).
- Tier: the verdict on a user driver is STATISTICAL; `--self-test` is
  DETERMINISTIC.

### inlining-budget-diff (inlining-budget-diff.sh)

Question: did the TurboFan / Maglev inlining DECISIONS for NAMED functions
change, plus a budget report?

    ME=m0 inlining-budget-diff.sh [opts] DRIVER_BEFORE DRIVER_AFTER      # driver mode (any project)
    inlining-budget-diff.sh [opts] --before-ref REF --after-ref REF       # lite-signal: builds from git refs
    inlining-budget-diff.sh [opts] --before FILE --after FILE             # lite-signal: two Signal.js files

- Driver mode is the general one (function names from `--fn` or `$ME`).
  The ref and file modes are lite-signal-shaped: they expect Signal.js /
  Watch.js and a driver importing `./Signal.js`. Do not use them on other
  projects.
- Options specific to it: `--fn LIST`, `--tiers LIST` (`turbo`, `maglev`),
  `--only-fn`, `--concurrent`, `--driver FILE`, `--repo DIR`,
  `--no-bytecode`. Output goes to `--out DIR` (default `$OUTDIR`, else a
  timestamped dir under `$TMPDIR`); a rerun needs a fresh, new or empty
  `--out`.
- Verdict per tier: exit 0 SAME, 1 DIFF, 2 NO-VERDICT. The budget report is
  REPORTED and never moves the verdict.
- Node 22: the maglev tier is NO-VERDICT; use `--tiers turbo`.
- Tier: the verdict is STATISTICAL, the budget report is REPORTED. There is no
  live control in the test suite; only `--self-test` (canned trace text) is
  deterministic.

### allocation-diff (allocation-diff.sh)

Question: did the number of young-generation GC EVENTS inside a marked window
change? Counts of GC events, never bytes.

    allocation-diff.sh [opts] DRIVER_BEFORE DRIVER_AFTER     # diff: SAME / DIFF
    allocation-diff.sh [opts] --zero DRIVER                  # gate: ZERO / NONZERO
    allocation-diff.sh --self-test

- Diff mode only plus `--zero`; no ref mode and no file mode.
- Exit 0 SAME or ZERO, 1 DIFF or NONZERO, 2 NO-VERDICT.
- ZERO means less than one semi-space of young allocation in the
  window, not zero bytes. An allocation TurboFan scalar-replaces is not an
  allocation: ZERO is then the correct reading.
- Driver contract: mark the window with
  `fs.writeSync(1, '@@LITE-MARK start\n')` and the same for `end`, written
  synchronously, before exit. Never use console.log or process.stdout in the
  driver. Warm up before `start`; a cold window over-reports.
- Tier: the script logic is DETERMINISTIC (`--self-test`); a verdict on a user
  driver is STATISTICAL and REPORTED only.

## Exit codes and the VERDICT line

| tool                  | 0                  | 1                 | 2          |
|-----------------------|--------------------|-------------------|------------|
| bytecode-budget       | WITHIN / REPORTED / SAME | OVER / DIFF | NO-VERDICT |
| deopt-diff            | SAME               | DIFF              | NO-VERDICT |
| ic-diff               | SAME               | DIFF              | NO-VERDICT |
| inlining-budget-diff  | SAME               | DIFF              | NO-VERDICT |
| allocation-diff       | SAME / ZERO        | DIFF / NONZERO    | NO-VERDICT |

Every run that reaches a verdict ends in a `VERDICT <v>` line on stdout. A refusal prints
`<tool>: <why>` and `VERDICT NO-VERDICT` on stderr and exits 2. A SIGINT /
SIGTERM / SIGHUP during a run ends NO-VERDICT, exit 2. `-h` exits 2.
`--self-test` exits 0 (all checks ok) or 1 (a FAIL line); that 1 is not DIFF.

## Tiers

- DETERMINISTIC: same inputs give the same verdict. bytecode-budget (one node
  binary), each tool's `--self-test`, the deopt-diff natives pair.
- STATISTICAL: the verdict on a user driver follows warm-up, GC and tier-up
  timing (deopt-diff, ic-diff, inlining-budget-diff, allocation-diff). Run
  them on a quiet host. These tools report; they do not gate a build.
- REPORTED: printed measurements that gate nothing (inlining budget report,
  deopt-diff tier section, allocation-diff counts line).

## Requirements

- bash >= 3.2.
- A POSIX awk (BSD awk and the ubuntu-latest awk are what the CI matrix uses;
  other awks are not claimed).
- node >= 22, with the ic-diff and inlining-budget-diff caveats above.
- git, for ref and file modes.
- `sha256sum` or `shasum`.
- No runtime npm dependencies.

## Known limits

Each bullet names its LEDGER id.

- an inherited SHELLOPTS=noexec runs nothing and exits 0; callers must require the VERDICT line, not only the exit code
  (#124)
- #126: some refusals of a non-path option value (an unknown option, a bad --fn / --v8-flags / --runs / --max /
  --node-version value, a node binary that is not found) print that raw value, so a CR or newline in it reaches stderr;
  exit 2, no verdict change.
- #66: `--v8-flags` numeric values are checked for FORM only; a value such as `=NaN` passes the check, node then fails,
  and the tool ends NO-VERDICT.
- #83: ic-diff on node 22 and 24 ends NO-VERDICT; a NO-VERDICT, never a wrong verdict.
- #122: a refusal may print a name that git or readlink resolved; a CR or newline in it (behind a symlink with a clean
  name) reaches stderr inside that refusal; exit 2.
- #84: allocation-diff does not strip NODE_NO_WARNINGS (it strips four other names); it can move the GC count.
- #76 (1), #80: inlining-budget-diff leaves its `--out` contents behind after some refusals; a rerun needs a fresh
  `--out`.
- #123: inlining-budget-diff file mode decides its "byte-identical, null control" NOTE on Signal.js alone; a differing
  Watch.js can print that NOTE and then DIFF. The verdict is right, the NOTE is false.
- Driver output is trusted (#72 B1b, #92 b): a driver can write lines that look like trace or marker output.
- a hard link to `--before` elsewhere in the repository (outside `--before`'s directory and below), or under a case-only
  sibling name on a case-sensitive file system, can stay undetected (LEDGER #71, #88, #89)
- Not a security boundary: the argument refusals are fail-closed hygiene, not a sandbox.

## Composability

One CI job can run all five. Gate only on bytecode-budget `--max` (exit 1 or 2
fails the job). Run the other four so a nonzero exit does not abort the job,
keep `--out` as an artifact, and fail the job if the `VERDICT` line is missing:

    rc=0; ./node_modules/.bin/deopt-diff --fn add --out out/dd before.js after.js > dd.txt || rc=$?
    grep -q '^VERDICT ' dd.txt || exit 1

The statistical tools report; they do not gate. Call installed tools as
`./node_modules/.bin/<name>`.
